title: CoWorld-VLA: Thinking in a Multi-Expert World Model for Autonomous Driving
claim: Existing reasoning paradigms use no, textual, or single implicit intermediate reasoning; ours organizes multiple expert reasoning tokens that condition a diffusion planner.
layout: 4 panels left-to-right, dashed dividers, shared VLM stack bottom-to-top, last panel highlighted
description: Four side-by-side panels separated by dashed vertical lines, each showing a bottom-to-top data flow. Every panel starts with a street photo (Image) and a gray rounded box (Prompt, Ego status, Command) labeled Text. Arrows lead up into a teal VLM bar, then up to a dashed box holding a car-with-trajectory icon labeled Action. Panel (a) Direct Action Prediction has no intermediate reasoning. Panel (b) Textual CoT adds a gray Textual CoT box beside the action. Panel (c) Single-World Latent Reasoning adds a light-blue Single Implicit CoT box. Panel (d), Multi-Expert World Reasoning (Ours), is more elaborate: a VLM feeds a stack of colored Dyn-CoT (pink), Geo-CoT (yellow) and Sem-CoT (green) tokens and a Light Action Head. These feed a purple Fusion Diffusion Planner, which outputs the Action. The eye goes to the busier, colorful panel (d).
caption: Comparison of reasoning paradigms for VLA-based autonomous driving. (a) Direct action prediction maps multimodal inputs to actions without intermediate reasoning. (b) Textual CoT introduces language-based reasoning but may lose continuous spatio-temporal details. (c) Single-world latent reasoning relies on one implicit world representation, which may be incomplete or weakly coupled with actions. (d) CoWorld-VLA performs multi-expert world reasoning by organizing Latent CoT experts and using a fusion diffusion planner for trajectory generation.
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for end-to-end autonomous driving. However, existing reasoning mechanisms still struggle to provide planning-oriented intermediate representations: textual Chain-of-Thought (CoT) fails to preserve continuous spatiotemporal structure, while latent world reasoning remains difficult to use as a direct condition for action generation. In this paper, we propose CoWorld-VLA, a multi-expert world reasoning framework for autonomous driving, where world representations serve as explicit conditions to guide action planning. CoWorld-VLA extracts complementary world information through multi-source supervision and encodes it into expert tokens within the VLA, thereby providing planner-accessible conditioning signals. Specifically, we construct four types of tokens: semantic interaction, geometric structure, dynamic evolution, and ego trajectory tokens, which respectively model interaction intent, spatial structure, future temporal dynamics, and behavioral goals. During action generation, CoWorld-VLA employs a diffusion-based hierarchical multi-expert fusion planner, which is coupled with scene context throughout the joint denoising process to generate continuous ego trajectories. Experiments on NAVSIM v1 & v2 demonstrate future-scene modeling capability and strong planning performance, including collision avoidance and trajectory accuracy. Ablation studies further validate the complementarity of expert tokens and their effectiveness as planning conditions for action generation. Code will be available at https://github.com/AFARI-Research/CoWorld-VLA.
